title: HoldRecordV1 — one member's mesh hold, and what to put back when it ends
description: One JSON object per line (JSON Lines) in the hold-record file declared by the peerview role (`lifecycle_hold_records`, default /var/lib/peerview/hold-records.jsonl). Written when a peer is moved into a hold group; read by the console (Access banner, Holds page, Release action) and by `lifecycle-sweep.py --lane release`. THE RECORD IS THE RESTORE SOURCE OF TRUTH: the hold group's name is only the restore TARGET, `prior_groups` is the restore CONTENT, and a release restores exactly that list and nothing else. Canon: docs/design/membership-lifecycle-and-transfer.md §'Hold record', ADR 1136 D1 (clarified 2026-09-11), ADR 1089 (dormancy lane), ADR 1091 (security lane). NO SECRETS and NO PERSONAL DATA beyond the handle: no email, no name, no IP.

v.description: Record version. A reader that does not recognise it refuses the line rather than guessing.

lane.description: Which kind of hold. `dormancy` = placed by the ADR 1136 inactivity sweep into the ADR 1089 PROBATION lane; releasable from the console. `security` = placed by an admin into the ADR 1091 QUARANTINED group; NEVER one-click releasable, exit is the close-out of an investigation. A peer in a hold group with NO record is treated as `security`.

site.description: Goatnet id (`site_id`), lowercase, e.g. `zagros`. Group names carry it upper-cased as their prefix.

peer_id.description: NetBird peer id — the stable key. Peer names can be edited; ids cannot.

peer_name.description: NetBird peer name at the time of the hold, as displayed (peer-name grammar: peer-<handle>-<short_tag>-<site>-<date>-<hostname>). Display only; never used as a key.

handle.description: The person's or device's handle, parsed from the peer name by the peer-name grammar. `null` when the name does not follow the grammar, or when the grammar leaves handle and short_tag ambiguous (both may contain hyphens and a writer without the registry cannot split them) — stated rather than invented, never a guess the console would match to the wrong member.

entered_at.description: When the hold was placed, UTC, second precision, trailing Z.

hold_group.description: The group the peer was moved INTO: `<SITE>-PROBATION-<role>` for `dormancy`, `<SITE>-QUARANTINED` for `security`. `<SITE>` is `site` upper-cased and MAY itself carry hyphens (`ZAGROS-PROD-QUARANTINED`, taxonomy `site_prefix`); the validator pins the prefix to `site`. Recorded so a reader does not have to derive the lane's group name.

prior_groups.description: Group NAMES the peer held immediately before the hold, excluding NetBird's implicit `All` and excluding the hold group itself. This is the restore content. May be empty (a peer that held only `All`); a release then removes the hold group and adds nothing.

actor.description: Who placed the hold: the literal `sweep` for the scheduled ADR 1136 run, otherwise the operator's handle. Never an email.

phase.description: Optional. Present only while a release of this record is in progress: the releaser rewrites the line with `phase: releasing` under the lock BEFORE it touches any group, so a release that dies half-way (prior groups restored, hold group not yet removed) is distinguishable from a hold that died half-way (hold group added, prior groups not yet removed) — the two are the same live shape. A reader treats a `releasing` record as a release to finish (`lifecycle-sweep.py --lane release --peer <id>` again), never as a stranded hold to complete. Absent = held.

reason.description: Optional short human-readable reason, e.g. `inactive 17d (person threshold 14d)`. For `security` holds keep it minimal — the record is readable by every ADMIN, and ADR 1091 minimises signal about an investigation.
